members.name: persuasion_v0

criteria.greeting: Opening social pleasantry: saying hello, asking how the partner is, or saying it is nice to meet them.
criteria.greeting_reply: Answering the partner's how-are-you with how the persuader is doing, including a short reply that they are doing the same, as part of the opening exchange.
criteria.closing: Ending the conversation without any thanks: wishing the partner a good day or night, saying goodbye, nice talking to you. (If it thanks the partner, choose thank.)
criteria.source_inquiry: Asks if the persuadee is familiar with the organization: whether they have heard of it or what they already know of it.
criteria.task_inquiry: Asks the persuadee's opinions, feelings, experience or habits about donating, charities, volunteering, children's causes, or the issues the charity addresses; or asks if they want more information or have questions about it.
criteria.personal_inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's own life unrelated to charity: their family, children, location, job, day, hobbies.
criteria.org_description: Describes the organization: its mission, programs, what it does, where it works, its history or founding.
criteria.org_trust: Vouches for the organization's legitimacy, reputation or scale: ratings, how much of the money goes to programs, transparency, being reputable or trustworthy, its accomplishments, funds raised, or how many children it has reached or helped.
criteria.website: Points the persuadee to the organization's website or a link for more information.
criteria.logical: Gives a reason or argument why donating makes sense: the donation will help children or make a difference, what donations or money gathered from many people accomplish, that contributions added together go a long way, the money goes to a good use, the cost to the persuadee is small compared to the benefit, everyone should help, children are the future.
criteria.emotion_suffering: Describes children's suffering, danger or death (hunger, war, disease, separation from families), including statistics of deaths or injuries, to evoke sympathy.
criteria.emotion_feeling: Expresses or evokes feelings (sadness, heartbreak, guilt, hope, feeling good about helping), including the persuader's own guilt or sorrow about others' hardship compared with their own comfort, or asks the persuadee to imagine a child's situation.
criteria.foot_in_door: Makes giving feel easy by shrinking what the persuadee themself is asked for: tells them that even a small or tiny donation from them helps or makes a difference, that a little is fine, or proposes a small or smaller specific sum to start with.
criteria.donation_info: Procedural facts about how the donation works in this task: it comes out of the task payment, how much can be given (the allowed range, that any amount up to the full payment is allowed), when or where to enter it, that the research team gathers the donations and forwards them to the charity, payment methods.
criteria.proposition: Directly asks or urges the persuadee to donate (would you donate, please donate, consider giving some of your payment).
criteria.ask_amount: Any question asking how much the persuadee wants, would like or is willing to donate, whether or not they have agreed to donate yet.
criteria.confirm_amount: Confirms or repeats back an amount the persuadee has already agreed to donate.
criteria.self_modeling: The persuader states that they themselves donate, will donate or volunteer, as an example to follow: their intention to donate in this chat, matching the persuadee, or their general habit of giving or volunteering (including answering yes when asked if they donate).
criteria.own_reasoning: The persuader reflects on their own personal reasons or decisions about giving, or their own preferences, without stating that they donate, without expressing feelings such as guilt or sadness, and without describing children's suffering or urging the persuadee.
criteria.personal_story: Narrates a specific episode: something that happened to the persuader or someone they know at a particular place or time, or the story of a specific child.
criteria.thank: Thanks the persuadee for their donation, help, time or chat.
criteria.praise: Compliments the persuadee personally: their kindness, generosity, being a good person, their decision to donate.
criteria.acknowledge: Neutral acknowledgement of what the persuadee just said: plain agreement, understanding, saying yes, okay, true, indeed, I know. No evaluation or emotion.
criteria.reaction: Evaluative or emotional reaction to what the persuadee said: calling it great, wonderful or amazing, being glad to hear it, being sorry to hear it, sympathizing, saying me too about oneself.
criteria.off_task: Talk unrelated to the charity or donation: small talk about other topics, the study or HIT mechanics, typos, jokes, celebrities, weather.
criteria.other: Anything else: the persuader's own opinions or answers to the persuadee's questions that fit no other option, fragments, unclear or non-English messages.

members.name: persuasion_v1
members.instructions: A persuader is chatting with someone to convince them to give money to Save the Children. Classify the persuader's last message (marked as the message to tag) by the dialogue act or persuasion strategy it performs. Earlier turns are context only. If the message does several things, pick the act that carries its main intent.
